title.narrative: VOLUNTARY CONTRIBUTION TO THE INTERNATIONAL SEABED AUTHORITY

description.narrative: Il contributo volontario ai Fondi Fiduciari Volontari dell'Autorità Internazionale dei Fondali Marini è destinato a sostenere la partecipazione dei delegati dei Paesi in via di sviluppo al lavoro del Consiglio e dei suoi organi sussidiari (Commissione Legale e Tecnica e Comitato per la Finanza). Questo sostegno mira a garantire un processo decisionale equilibrato, inclusivo e rappresentativo nella governance dell'Autorità, assicurando che le decisioni da essa prese tengano adeguatamente conto delle esigenze e delle specificità dei paesi in via di sviluppo, in particolare per quanto riguarda la protezione ambientale dell'ambiente marino e la condivisione equa dei benefici derivanti dallo sfruttamento delle risorse minerarie.

The voluntary contribution to the Voluntary Trust Funds of the International Seabed Authority is intended to support the participation of delegates from Developing Countries in the work of the Council and its subsidiary bodies (Legal and Technical Commission and Finance Committee). This support aims to ensure a balanced, inclusive and representative decision-making process in the governance of the Authority, ensuring that decisions taken by it adequately take into account the needs and specificities of developing countries, particularly with regard to the environmental protection of the marine environment and the equitable sharing of benefits derived from the exploitation of mineral resources.

tag.narrative: By 2025, prevent and significantly reduce marine pollution of all kinds, in particular from land-based activities, including marine debris and nutrient pollution
By 2030, progressively achieve and sustain income growth of the bottom 40 per cent of the population at a rate higher than the national average
Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development

Enhance the conservation and sustainable use of oceans and their resources by implementing international law as reflected in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, which provides the legal framework for the conservation and sustainable use of oceans and their resources, as recalled in paragraph 158 of “The future we want”

Increase scientific knowledge, develop research capacity and transfer marine technology, taking into account the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission Criteria and Guidelines on the Transfer of Marine Technology, in order to improve ocean health and to enhance the contribution of marine biodiversity to the development of developing countries, in particular small island developing States and least developed countries
Reduce inequality within and among countries
Strengthen domestic resource mobilization, including through international support to developing countries, to improve domestic capacity for tax and other revenue collection
Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the global partnership for sustainable development
